elements.element: Vendor has an express duty to defend Customer and its affiliates.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1 chapeau: "RevMed shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless Sanofi, its Affiliates and their respective officers, directors, agents and employees ('Sanofi Indemnitees')" — express defend obligation running to Customer and its Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims.
elements.evidence: 14.1: "from and against any Third Party Claims and Losses arising therefrom under or related to this Agreement"; "Third Party Claims" is defined at 1.126 and "Losses" at 1.60.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers claims that Services or Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: New limb (d): "any allegation that the services performed or deliverables provided by RevMed under this Agreement, the RevMed Licensed Technology, or the Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product ... infringe or misappropriate the intellectual property rights of any Third Party". The deterministic check "vendor indemnity for IP infringement present: false" reflects the pre-edit baseline/model wording pattern, not the rendered text, which plainly carries the infringement limb in operative language.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: New limb (e): "RevMed's breach of Applicable Law"; "Applicable Law" is a defined term (Section 1.8 per the drafter's note), so no dangling term is created.

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: New limb (f): "any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Sanofi's Confidential Information or other data of Sanofi caused by RevMed".

elements.element: Vendor indemnity covers Vendor's gross negligence and wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.1(a): "the negligence, recklessness or willful misconduct of any of the RevMed Indemnitees" — simple negligence necessarily subsumes gross negligence, and wilful misconduct is named.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.3(a): "The Indemnified Party will give the indemnifying Party ... prompt written notice (an 'Indemnification Claim Notice') of any Losses ... under Section 14.1 or Section 14.2", with failure-to-notify prejudice qualifier preserved.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure allocates control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Retained 14.3(b) Control of Defense: "the Indemnifying Party may assume the defense of any Third Party Claim ... by giving written notice ... may select and appoint the lead legal counsel".

elements.element: The indemnification procedure requires reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Retained cooperation paragraph: "the Indemnified Party will ... cooperate in the defense thereof and will furnish such records, information and testimony ... as may be reasonably requested", with Vendor reimbursement of out-of-pocket costs.

elements.element: Customer indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: 14.2 as rewritten reads only "(a) content, data or materials provided by Sanofi to RevMed; or (b) Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law; (c) [Intentionally omitted]; (d) [Intentionally omitted]" — the prior Research/Development/Manufacture/Commercialization, warranty-breach and obligation-breach limbs are gone.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party intellectual-property claims.
elements.evidence: Same new 14.1(d) infringement/misappropriation limb in favour of the Sanofi Indemnitees.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element: no modification exclusion is inserted, which is at least as favourable to Customer as the fallback tolerates; the retained carve-out chapeau ((i)-(iii)) is Sanofi-fault based, so nothing contradicts this element.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer combinations.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no combination exclusion is added and none is required for the fallback to be satisfied.

elements.element: The IP indemnity may exclude infringement caused by Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: Permissive element; no specification exclusion appears in the rendered 14.1 exception chapeau.

elements.element: Vendor must procure continued use, modify, or replace the infringing item.
elements.evidence: No mitigation/remedy mechanic anywhere in the rendered 14.1-14.3; the redline adds only indemnity limbs. To reach the fallback the drafter would have to insert an express obligation for RevMed to procure the right to continue, modify or replace the infringing item.

elements.element: Vendor must refund applicable fees if procure, modify, or replace remedies are unavailable.
elements.evidence: No refund fallback remedy is drafted; there is no operative sentence conditioning a refund on the unavailability of procure/modify/replace.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity is subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3x annual fees super-cap is inserted; the drafter deliberately left the indemnity uncapped under Section 14.5, which is why only the preferred level is targeted.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all ten preferred elements are met on the rendered operative language (limbs (d)-(f) added, 14.2 narrowed to Sanofi-provided content and Sanofi's breach of Applicable Law, and the notice / control-of-defence / cooperation machinery in 14.3 retained verbatim).

The failing deterministic check 'vendor indemnity for IP infringement present' does not defeat element 3 on substance: the rendered 14.1(d) contains an express allegation-of-infringement/misappropriation limb; the regex evidently tests the pre-edit baseline or the model phrase 'Services or Deliverables'.

Fallback is not complete (procure/modify/replace, refund and 3x super-cap are all absent), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is met; note the redline gives up nothing by not adding the super-cap.

Minimality fails on the breadth of new limb (d). The checklist element is limited to infringement by the Vendor's services or deliverables; adapting it to 'the RevMed Licensed Technology' is a fair terminology mapping, but 'or the Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product in accordance with this Agreement' extends the indemnity to Sanofi's own downstream conduct and converts the clause into a full freedom-to-operate indemnity outside the checklist. Repair: delete the words 'or the Research, Development, Manufacture or Commercialization of any SHP2 Inhibitor or Product in accordance with this Agreement' from 14.1(d), leaving '...the services performed or deliverables provided by RevMed under this Agreement or the RevMed Licensed Technology, infringe or misappropriate the intellectual property rights of any Third Party'.

The conforming change of the exception chapeau from '(a) through (c)' to '((a) through (f))' is accepted as necessary cross-reference maintenance (and is Vendor-favourable, not an added Customer requirement), so it is not counted as a separate minimality defect.

Intent is preserved on the visible text: the '[Intentionally omitted]' placeholders keep 14.2's lettering stable, no cross-reference is left dangling, and 'Applicable Law', 'Third Party', 'Losses', 'Product' and 'SHP2 Inhibitor' are defined. Two confirmations for the drafter: (i) verify 'RevMed Licensed Technology' is a defined term as used in limb (d); and (ii) confirm the broad limb (d) does not contradict any retained third-party-IP/licence cost-sharing mechanic (e.g. Article 12 third-party infringement or the Profit/Loss Share Agreement) — narrowing limb (d) as above also removes that conflict risk.

Section 13.5's non-infringement warranty disclaimer is not contradicted by an indemnity limb, but if the parties push back, point out that 14.1(d) is a claim-allocation provision rather than a warranty.
